title: ID0465498-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] EVSE Module Fault
description: Reported Behaviour/ Issue: EVSE Module Fault

additional_info.subject: Escalation on repeated EVSE module faults at Brite site 170003301
additional_info.body:
Dear Siemens team,
We are escalating repeated EVSE module faults on SICHARGE D unit 170003301 covering the period 26 November to 2 December 2025. While the charger consistently reports as Available and Online, EVSEs 2, 3 and 4 enter Faulted state multiple times with Siemens vendor error codes indicating internal module failures.
Below are the exact timestamps and vendor codes.
EVSE 3 faults
26 November 2025 17:12:41
InternalError
Status Faulted
27 November 2025 13:16:12
InternalError
27 November 2025 19:55:28
OtherError
VendorErrorCode evse is not ready
30 November 2025 12:39:30
OtherError
VendorErrorCode evse is not ready
30 November 2025 12:40:38
OtherError
VendorErrorCode evse is not ready
30 November 2025 16:14:02
OtherError
VendorErrorCode secc pilot is E
30 November 2025 16:14:04
InternalError
2 December 2025 07:30:08
InternalError
2 December 2025 10:14:30
InternalError
EVSE 2 faults
29 November 2025 19:26:31
OtherError
VendorErrorCode secc is offline
30 November 2025 13:20:20
OtherError
VendorErrorCode secc pilot is E
30 November 2025 13:20:30
InternalError
2 December 2025 11:59:16
InternalError
2 December 2025 14:43:14
InternalError
EVSE 4 faults
30 November 2025 15:57:28
InternalError
30 November 2025 22:37:08
OtherError
VendorErrorCode evse is not ready
1 December 2025 09:36:45
OtherError
VendorErrorCode evse is not ready
Requested actions from Siemens
Provide full interpretation of the vendor codes listed above for this SICHARGE D unit.
Identify any shared internal control modules across EVSEs 2, 3 and 4 which could explain fault propagation.
Confirm the likely root cause based on these timestamps.
Provide a technical remedy, which may include on site inspection, SECC board or cable replacement, firmware updates or module swap.
Confirm whether it is expected behaviour for the charger to show ChargePointStatus Available while multiple EVSEs are Faulted.
We request an urgent response due to the customer impact and operational cost associated with these repeated failures.
Regards,
Colin
Brite Charging

Hello Colin, good morning. Hope you are doing well.
Here is what I found for the several sessions:
EVSE 3 faults
26 November 2025 17:12:41
InternalError
Status Faulted
-> Why the customer couldn't start a session was due to a Transaction already ongoing:
27 November 2025 13:16:12
InternalError
-> In this case, there is no authentication method provided and the session aborts during Authentication phase.
27 November 2025 19:55:28
OtherError
VendorErrorCode evse is not ready
-> I checked this session and right before the session starts we have 0 Volts in the output
Right when the session starts, the EV connects and creates a hazard:
To ensure that there is no possibility of harm, the charger
must disable
this connector until the user plugs out. This is according to international norms, where it specifies that if the charging station sees a voltage on the output side without any charging ongoing it must stop.
As you can see below, as soon as the user plugs out the EV, the connector is available again:

-> Exactly like the same above, as soon as the EV plugs in, we see an output voltage and the charger stops immediately.
30 November 2025 12:40:38

VendorErrorCode evse is not ready
-> This is the same consequence as above since the user didn't plug out the EV, and as soon as he plugs out, the connector is available again:

additional_info.body:
Dear Service Coordinator / RC,
I am writing to inform that we are moving the case
0465498
﻿from the Technical Support to the eMobility RC-IE SI E Queue. We kindly ask you to take over the case and perform the necessary troubleshooting steps.
Customer: Brite
Product:
Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset:
MP / S2 170003301
Charger ID / Serial No.:3g38Q6
Charger address/functional location:
Priority:
High
Handover reason:
Check the KF11 connection to the switch, the error is very sporadic so there are 3 things to check:
Ethernet cable -> replace
Change Switch port
If all else fails and the problem persists, replace KF11
For the DC4 Voltage transducer problem, check if these wires are properly attached and reaching the KF202 properly. If the problem persists, you can try swapping TF203 with TF204 and if the problem persists in the same transducer, replace it. If the problem is now on the working transducer then it means we have a cabling problem.
Kindly pick up the case using "Pick" option in the queue or manually using the "Assign" function from the
eMobility RC-XX SI E Queue
and work on it & document the activity (Logs/Field Service Report) and attach it to the case under Documents Tab on ISP.
In case you require Expert Support, kindly create Work-order as per
unified service process

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0465498-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] EVSE Module Fault CRM:03055000399
additional_info.body:
Hello Francisco,
All good here, getting ready for Santa in our house!!
So, thanks a million for the detailed review and for going through each of the timestamps we sent. Really appreciate the clarity you provided around the user-side issues, especially the cases where:
• No authentication method was presented
• The wrong connector ID was selected in the app
• A session was already ongoing, blocking a new start
It is very helpful to have those confirmed, and we will make sure our own support team and signage reflect this.
Just a couple of follow-ups from our side to help complete the picture when you have a bit more time to dig in.
The repeated EVSE module faults you highlighted
We see from your breakdown that EVSEs 2, 3 and 4 are entering Faulted state with the following patterns:
EVSE 4
30 November 15:57:28 InternalError
30 November 22:37:08 Faulted – VendorErrorCode “evse is not ready”
1 December 09:36:45 Faulted – VendorErrorCode “evse is not ready”
EVSE 3
27 November 13:16:12 InternalError
30 November 13:20:30 InternalError
EVSE 2
2 December 11:59:16 InternalError
2 December 14:43:14 InternalError
These are the ones we are most concerned about because they repeat even when no user is attempting a session.
Vendor error code interpretation
When you get a chance, could you share a short interpretation of
• “evse is not ready”
• “secc pilot is E”
• repeated InternalError states
We just want to understand whether these typically point to SECC-side issues, pilot signal stability, internal communications, or something environmental.
Next diagnostic step
There is absolutely no rush, but when your deeper analysis is complete, it would be great to know whether you think this will require
a) remote adjustments or firmware
or
b) an eventual on-site check of the modules.
We completely understand you need time to correlate all the data, and we appreciate the work you are doing on this.
Let me know if you need any additional logs or event exports from our side. More than happy to send whatever makes your job easier.
Thanks again Francisco,
Colin
Brite Charging
